packages.name: @parya/design-system
packages.description: React components, foundations, hooks and page templates.

releases.title: Horizontal logo and documentation polish

items: Replaced the four horizontal logo colors with the supplied full Paryatech wordmark including P.
Updated the documentation header and shared AppShell logo to the supplied artwork.
Refreshed original downloads, per-format dimensions, SHA-256 hashes and ZIP packs.
Simplified the documentation top bar to the logo, wider search and utility controls; navigation stays in the sidebar.
Removed the preview version and React/TypeScript labels from the sidebar.
Emphasized documentation resources with teal actions and a primary Copy for LLM button.
A searchable gallery for all 151 Paper icons, available from the sidebar and the Icon component page; select an icon to copy its React usage.

releases.adoption: The asset filenames and component APIs are unchanged. PNG downloads are 2385 × 517 pixels; SVG artboards are 1193 × 259.

releases.title: Phone layouts and brand assets

items: Labelled table cards preserve sorting and selection in narrow containers; scrolling tables remain available.
Phone navigation uses a focus-managed dialog. Page layouts, forms, board stage navigation and schedule week navigation adapt to smaller screens.
The playground Phone preview renders in an actual phone viewport.
Package-specific version history, adoption notes and generated release documentation.
Matching editable 390px Paper references and a release ledger.
Ten supplied stacked-logo, standalone-symbol and app-tile variants: 14 additional original files, grouped previews, exact colors and refreshed download packs.

releases.adoption: DataTable defaults to cards below 600px container width; use mobileLayout="scroll" for wide comparisons. KanbanBoard defaults to phone stage navigation; use mobileLayout="snap" for swipe-only navigation. No public API is removed.

releases.title: Collection workflows and practical foundations

items: FilterMenu, FilterChips, SortMenu, ListToolbar, ListPageTemplate and IconTextCell.
Typography roles, color guidance, contrast checks and generated foundation documentation.
Controlled table sorting and selection across pages; typed utility documentation and shared examples.

releases.adoption: filterRows ignores groups without an accessor. paginate clamps pages beyond the last page; invalid page numbers and sizes still throw. sortRows keeps empty values last in both directions.

releases.title: Initial experimental implementation

items: Paper tokens and SVG icon inventory; React components and shared examples.
Documentation site, source/Paper links, generated API tables, Markdown and LLM references.
Four reusable hooks and a separate connected Storybook application.

releases.adoption: Install from the repository or a locally packed archive. This recorded preview version was not published to npm.

releases.title: Corrected horizontal logo

items: Uses the corrected horizontal wordmark through @parya/design-system 0.3.1.

releases.adoption: Uses the shared library 0.3.1 through the existing repository dependency.

releases.title: Phone APIs and workspace stories

items: Application shell and keyboard selection examples.
Shared workspace, content, notification, calendar, chart, pricing and template stories.
API documentation synchronized with the library phone layouts and schedule week navigation.

releases.adoption: Uses @parya/design-system 0.3.0 through the shared repository dependency. Run sync after updating the library. This remains a private application.

releases.title: Shared component and foundation stories

items: Stories for the shared v0.2 collection controls, foundation roles and typed examples.
QuantityField controls synchronized with the shared API.

releases.adoption: Run sync after changing shared examples. This is a private application, not a separately published component library.

publication: Recorded preview versions. The component library is not published to npm; Storybook is a private application.
templateNote: Templates own page spacing. Phone layouts reuse the same template slots, semantic tokens and components; smaller screens change their arrangement.
